executiveSummary: GM0353's 2025 identity, centre, 33,339-person control, 31 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three BRT settlement labels and three logical road records are internally coherent; the neighbourhood population sum differs by one (+0.003%) and is correctly reconciled without rewriting observations. The complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The river preset rises from zero to exactly 1.346752 m by T+12 and holds identical depth, severity, affected population, pressure and service availability through T+72, without selecting a Lek level, Lopikerwaard defence state, breach, probability, connected footprint, arrival or recession. One LIWO point named Lek km 952.5 (IJsselstein) is a scenario-catalogue candidate, not an active or selected breach. Eight active T+24 presets reuse the same neighbourhood ordering, placing official Lage Dijk pluvial/heat hotspots near the bottom and failing to represent Binnenstad, Zenderpark, IJsselveld and Europakwartier evidence. Public water/sewer assets, high-groundwater monitoring, road/tram context, cross-boundary acute care, schools, antennas and utility-provider/planning data remain non-causal context. The first 72 hours need a pre-impact evacuation/safe-shelter contract, event-valid A2/N210/tram/care access and typed water-service dependencies. No public source establishes current defence, route, facility, utility or restoration state; Unknown and NoData must never be shown as zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0353 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0353 as IJsselstein in Utrecht and reports 33,339 residents, density 1,587/km², 20.4% aged 65 or older and 4,732 one-person households; the generated centre [5.027876128335938,52.03202789273353] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Thirty-one neighbourhood rows in one district sum to 33,340 residents, one above the municipality total (+0.003%); households sum to 14,445 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 6,800. Allocation reconciles to 33,339 without rewriting source observations.

BAG supplies the active woonplaats IJsselstein and BRT supplies IJsselstein woonkern plus Achtersloot and Klaphek buurtschappen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0; labels do not establish occupancy or hazard exposure.

The generated overview polygon has 60 coordinate positions versus 1,734 in the fresh non-generalized feature. Average home value/cars per household cover 26/31, several housing fields 27/31, benefits 28/31, doctor/supermarket distance 30/31, and district heat/charging 0/31; null and suppressed values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Visie en uitvoeringsprogramma Klimaatadaptatie IJsselstein 2023–2028
evidenceSources.edition: Plan dated 16 March 2023, adopted November 2023; public document inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted plan combines 2021/2022 regional stress tests, a 2019 peak-rain study and a local detailed scan. It identifies rain problems at Bep Belostraat, Herman Benschopstraat, Wim Hoogendoornstraat, Jan de Kuijerstraat, Gerbrandytoren, Biezenplein, Lage Dijk around Zeemanlaan/Lorentzlaan, roads under 90 mm/day and potential loss of access in Europakwartier; resident-dialogue locations require further research rather than being treated as confirmed depths.

Binnenstad and Zenderpark are heat hotspots; Lage Dijk and Boerhaave have little cooling and dark flat roofs, while Lage Dijk and IJsselveld have long distances to cool places. Long heat can affect movable bridges at Poortdijk and Oranje Nassaulaan. These are static stress-test/planning findings, not observations or operational restrictions.

Drought evidence identifies older wooden foundations mainly in Binnenstad and older homes northeast of it, road/sewer subsidence, rural desiccation between Zuid IJsseldijk and Achtersloot, a manually controlled spindle at sportpark IJsseloever and possible future subsidence near Groenvliet/De Wereldsteden. Groundwater insight was sparse in 2023; dated scenario ranges are not current measurements.

The plan describes Hollandse IJssel through the city, Kromme/Enge IJssel south and Lek farther south; a dated medium-probability map showed spatially variable flooding, including up to about one metre in IJsselveld/IJsselwetering. It says preventive evacuation may not always be possible and calls for evacuation above 0.5 m or nearby dry upper-floor shelter when time is insufficient, while calamity roles and critical/vulnerable-object mapping were still work in progress.

The PDF is a static adopted plan with no machine refresh or standard reuse licence stated. Its low nature-fire assessment is relative to the national picture and acknowledges dispersed vulnerability and possible verge fires; it is not a live all-clear.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Water- en rioleringsprogramma and current groundwater monitoring context
evidenceSources.edition: Registry filename 2024–2028; adopted by council as WRP 2025–2028 in October 2024; groundwater webpage inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The WRP covers municipal wastewater, rain, groundwater and surface-water duties and examines dangerous discharges, sewer-pump outage, pressure-pipe breaks, main-sewer collapse under important roads and extreme-rain waterlogging. Indirect industrial discharges can block or damage sewers, pumps and RWZI operation; HDSR gives this priority.

The municipality reports high groundwater and a local digital monitoring network measured automatically several times daily, while also warning that values vary locally and its duty concerns public space. The programme inventory referred to roughly twenty meters; neither source establishes complete parcel coverage or a current municipality-wide groundwater state.

The programme requires 40–70 mm private-site storage for new building and uses measuring/monitoring, but exposes no public connected sewer/catchment topology, unit-compatible pump capacity, event state, backup, dangerous-discharge incident, main-road failure or restoration commitment.

Both sources are public municipal policy/display context; no standard reuse licence, fixed machine delivery contract or incident SLA was identified. The title-period discrepancy is retained rather than silently normalized.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Jaarsveld–Klaphek Lekdijk project, Gekanaliseerde Hollandsche IJssel level decision and climate-resilient water supply
evidenceSources.edition: Final dike project decision 29 October 2025; GHIJ level decision adopted 25 February 2026; current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The Jaarsveld–Klaphek project covers approximately 9.2–9.5 km from the IJsselstein border toward Jaarsveld. More than four kilometres had been strengthened and further execution was expected from late 2026/2027; traffic planning includes temporary dike closures and N210 connections. Project phase does not establish current failure probability, breach or passability.

The final decision specifies a 670 m piping screen at Klaphek/IJsseldam and describes the primary Lekdijk between Amerongen and Schoonhoven as protecting much of central/western Netherlands under 2017 standards. This is bounded design/project evidence, not a selected flood scenario or present strength claim.

HDSR's 25 February 2026 Gekanaliseerde Hollandsche IJssel decision describes the waterway through historic IJsselstein as important for freshwater conveyance during drought and drainage in normal/wet periods. During severe drought, Koekoek can take Lek water into Lopikerwaard and De Aanvoerder can convey it west, sometimes for months around the clock; this is contingency context, not current operation.

Public pages provide dated regional system and project evidence but no standard machine incident cadence or standard redistribution licence identified. Defence, level-control, pumping and route state remain Unknown without an authority-selected event.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regional risk/crisis plans, LIWO 2025 breach catalogue and Waterinfo point context
evidenceSources.edition: VRU risk profile 2023; crisis plan 2024–2027; LIWO 2025.1.6; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: VRU treats river flooding as catastrophic and highlights mass evacuation, continuity and resource scarcity. It separates rain, storm, heat/drought, nature fire, vital-infrastructure and cyber risks, including electricity cascades to road/water/rail and cyber dependencies of energy, drinking water and water systems; the crisis plan distinguishes acute, forecast and prolonged action clocks.

Exact containment against the full GM0353 boundary finds one LIWO primary candidate, Lek km 952.5 (IJsselstein) at [5.0674,51.9946], with catalogue flags in two probability-band fields and no regional, regional-water-system or outer-dike candidate match. It is a professional scenario entry requiring water-manager selection, not an active breach, probability estimate or footprint; empty categories do not mean safe.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast is assigned inside GM0353. Nieuwegein Doorslag is nearest at 4.24 km, with 2.2 m³/s discharge and 60 cm NAP at 16:50Z on 2 September 2026; Hagestein beneden is farther away. Point levels/flows are not dike state or inundation and may not be silently aligned to synthetic T+0.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute observations and a public non-mission-critical service; forecast frontend semantics require validation and no local T+72 series is available. LIWO is versioned/irregular with layer-specific resolution, units, NoData and licensing; VRU documents are dated public governance evidence without machine incident cadence or standard reuse licence stated.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB road gateways, Regiotram/GTFS and timestamped road-situation context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; NDW snapshot 2 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has three mobility/supply-only logical records: A2 and N210 toward Nieuwegein and N210 toward Lopik. The two N210 records share one physical corridor and nominal 150 values are non-additive synthetic capacity units, not measured emergency throughput.

There is no conventional ProRail station, but Province Utrecht owns/manages the Regiotram and Transdev/U-OV runs line 21 from IJsselstein via Nieuwegein and Utrecht CS to Science Park. OVapi GTFS version 9543, retrieved 31 August under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, supplies 27 in-boundary stop areas and eight nearby line-21 shapes; geometry/schedule does not establish journeys, ridership, accessibility or event operation.

The nearest assigned NDW situation is about 2.96 km from the municipality reference point, timestamped 2 September 2026 and low-severity stationary traffic. It neither validates A2/N210/dike-road/tram passability at synthetic scenario time nor proves absence of disruption.

NWB, GTFS and NDW have different time, coverage, quality and licence semantics. Event-valid direction, physical corridor identity, closure, flood intersection, bridge state, destination and Unknown capacity must be retained separately.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-asset, provider-responsibility and electricity-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; provider records updated 7 September 2025–24 March 2026
supports: Exact full-boundary assignment finds 115 HWH objects: 104 weirs, nine surface-water pumps, one sewer pump and RWZI Nieuwegein. The pump register includes drainage/intake/underdrain roles and some null capacities. HWH Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0; points do not establish connected topology, compatible units, power, live state, backup or restoration.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point queries identify Stedin electricity (updated 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025) and Vitens drinking water (7 September 2025), while drainage and telecom return empty. Provider polygons are responsibility context rather than physical topology, outage, coverage or restoration; empty responses remain Unknown.

One NBNL postcode sample at 3401GX maps to Stedin station TS068_10 IJsselstein and reports null existing/required withdrawal and injection values, queues of 4.8 MW/12 requests and 0.5 MW/6 requests, 29 projects and earliest year 2028.

NBNL planning/queue data updates at least quarterly/monthly with no exact standard licence identifier found and is not complete municipal coverage, live load, emergency spare capacity, switching, outage or restoration. Null capacity values remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public communications, education, acute-care, air, weather and seismic context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: RDI assigns 39 antenna installations—eleven mobile, five fixed-link, eighteen amateur, three broadcast and two other-mobile—and daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns seventeen education locations: eleven primary, two secondary and four other registered. Registers do not establish coverage, occupancy, shelter role, backup or operation; RDI licence/cadence is unstated.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 has no point in GM0353. St. Antonius Nieuwegein is nearest to the reference point at 3.70 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 emergency department, eighteen treatment rooms and 22,094 visits in 2025 but no acute obstetrics; this is dated questionnaire context, not route time, diversion, staffing, occupancy or guaranteed capacity.

No KNMI observation station lies inside; Cabauw is nearest at 9.88 km in the retrieved ten-minute CC BY 4.0 snapshot. No RIVM PM2.5 point lies inside; Cabauw is nearest at 9.60 km. No seismic origin lies inside the 365-day CC BY 4.0 query; the nearest retrieved event was induced M1.72 Noordbeemster at 60.35 km.

No-match is not zero local weather, air exposure or earthquake hazard, and point distance does not establish representativeness. Event-time values, coverage, quality flags, units, issue/valid time, licence and NoData must remain explicit.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A source-free river scalar and common neighbourhood seed conflict with local flood, rain, heat, drought and access evidence.
notes: River depth rises from zero at T+0 to 0.474057 m at T+6 and 1.346752 m at T+12, then remains exactly identical through T+72 without a selected Lek level, defence/breach, connected raster, arrival or recession.

Official pluvial evidence instead identifies Lage Dijk, named streets, surface-water bottlenecks and Europakwartier access; heat evidence distinguishes Binnenstad, Zenderpark, Lage Dijk, Boerhaave and IJsselveld. Lage Dijk ranks 30th under the common model seed and Binnenstad eighth.

Administrative centres/common seeds cannot substitute for selected hydraulic cells, defence/elevation, rain-sewer surface, imperviousness, shade, groundwater, demographics, source/target or exposed-object geometry.

The 115 HWH objects and municipal sewer/groundwater evidence do not form a connected surface-water/sewer/pump/RWZI graph or affect drainage/water restoration.
Provider territories and one NBNL sample cannot support exact electricity, water, gas or telecom availability; line 21, external ED, schools and antennas have no continuity/dependency edges.

notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.

Public layers correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; trace does not select a stress-test edition, LIWO footprint, defence state, water observation, route/tram state, facility state, occupancy or utility topology.

A foreseeable flood needs pre-impact warning and separate evacuation, safe-shelter, closure, rescue, care-transfer, pumping/dewatering and re-entry decisions; the current scenario begins at T+0 without an event-specific lead-time ledger.
Actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent disruption is conservative, but exact T+12–72 river constancy and T+24–72 service plateaus are not locally calibrated.
notes: River T+72 retains exactly 1.346752 m, severity 0.420024, pressure 0.530433, 18,339 affected and 1,068,472.214 person-hours; availability ranges from drainage 0.246478 to gas 0.707951 and is unchanged from T+24.

Compound T+72 retains 0.321779 depth/stress, 23,121 affected and 1,277,593.770 person-hours; telecom is 0.159058 and supply 0.294159. Affected residents, depth, pressure and services exactly plateau after T+24 while severity falls.
Dike, GHIJ, pumps, sewers, bridges, A2/N210/tram, care and utility evidence supports dependencies but does not validate these exact values or restoration commitments.
Keep conservative repair blocking as a synthetic exercise guard, expose uncertainty and do not imply a local promise until water compartments and action-valid recovery milestones are selected.

findings.summary: Sparse statistics and empty public queries remain Unknown rather than false zero or safe state.

Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain provider areas and NBNL quarterly/monthly planning are not topology, load or outage. DUO is daily attribution data, RIVM acute-care v1.1 is fixed CC0 questionnaire context and RDI licence/cadence is unstated. Request safe aggregate service zones, care referral, facility role, coverage, backup and restoration bands; unavailable or sensitive fields remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee or operator commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality total; null statistics, provider, capacity, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.
The 60-position overview is suitable for display/selection, not defence, hydraulic, rainfall, sewer, groundwater, terrain, asset, building or route intersection; use the full 1,734-position geometry.
The municipal climate/flood statements are dated planning/stress-test evidence, not current probability, live inundation, groundwater, bridge failure or a universal depth.
The contained LIWO point is a scenario-catalogue candidate, not an active breach or selected footprint; empty regional/outer-dike candidate queries do not prove safety.
Nearest Waterinfo, KNMI, RIVM air and NDW records are timestamped points/records outside or not assigned inside GM0353 and cannot be silently spatially or temporally aligned to synthetic T+0.
HDSR project and level-control evidence identifies tasks and system roles but not current failure, strength, pump/level state, road restriction or restoration time.
HWH's 115 points do not establish connected catchments, live pump/weir/RWZI state, compatible capacity, power, backup or restoration; contributor completeness varies.
NWB/NDW, GTFS, provider territories, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records do not establish live passability, operation, occupancy, physical topology, capacity, backup or repair.
Registered residents do not equal people at Lage Dijk, schools, tram stops, care sites, workplaces, recreation or events; incident-time occupancy is not consumed.

No complete public electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, stock, staffing, crew or restoration topology is consumed; unavailable/security-sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Direct coastal/fire/earthquake zero and catalogue/query no-match are narrow model/source statements, not no indirect coast, smoke, ignition, seismic, access or supply effect.

Recovery after T+72, pre-impact lead time, cross-boundary defence/service consequences, destinations, shelter/care capacity, mutual aid and resource constraints remain outside locally validated scope.
